column1: A condition for policy such as (8.49) that is derived from the central bank’s first-order conditions and only involves variables that appear in the objective function (in this case, inflation and the output gap) is generally called a targeting rule (e.g., Svensson and Woodford 2005). It represents a relationship among the targeted variables that the central bank should maintain, because doing so is consistent with the first-order conditions from its policy problem.
